info.title: Luma API
info.description: Read cases, evidence, proposals, execution and audit history. Make permitted decisions and follow authenticated progress streams. Manage organizations, memberships and installed connections. Organization endpoints require a session cookie.

get.summary: Read the latest Shadow evaluation for a case and Workflow
get.description: Returns the retained prediction, operator review and compatible authoritative outcome. Returns null when no evaluation is recorded.

post.summary: Evaluate a resolution in Shadow Mode
post.description: Evaluate the current diagnosis and bound Workflow proposal without executing it. Set workflow to the Workflow definition ID. Missing candidates are retained. Reuse the evaluation ID for exact retries.

Record the observed operator action, eligibility assessment and optional trust feedback with evidence from this incident. The first review is retained; conflicting retries return 409. Authoritative outcomes are read separately from verification history.

get.summary: Compare Shadow predictions with observed outcomes
get.description: People who can activate playbooks can compare up to 500 incidents for one Workflow within a time window. The latest evaluation per incident is counted. Rates include denominators and exclude unknown observations. Predictions are conditional simulations, not executed or verified resolutions.

Returns recorded events newest first by recorded timestamp and immutable ID. Date bounds apply to recorded time, including from and excluding to, for at most 366 days. Search matches issue ID, persisted target reference, action label, actor ID and workflow run ID (literal, case-insensitive substring). Raw payloads are not searched. Cursors are bound to workspace, restricted-activity access, filters and page size; any other cursor returns 400 with a message to start from the first page. Connection changes and access changes (members, invitations, roles and workspace settings, type `access`) are visible only with the View restricted activity permission; `visibility` is `admin` for those callers. Approval and provider acceptance do not establish verified resolution.
Requires `workflows.read`. People can inspect published versions and activation status. Viewing a playbook never activates it.
Read steps, versions, prerequisites and historical grants. Evaluation evidence is explicitly unavailable when no integrated evaluation source exists.
Returns the 50 most recent runs with issue links and separate execution and verification results. Pilot and unclassified evidence do not establish live success.

post.description: Requires `playbooks.activate`. Grants your own principal access to explicit orders on one connection. Review the exact digest, scope and approval behavior. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response. Conflicting, overlapping or stale grants return 409; revoked records cannot be restored.
Requires `playbooks.activate`. Prevents future admission under this artifact. Repeated revocation is safe. Revocation preserves historical grants and does not undo already-dispatched work.
Adds a subscription revision. Historical runs retain their exact subscription and immutable workflow version. Starts must review the current subscription revision.
Records the assignee’s answer and evidence once. Answers are workflow input; provider changes still require policy admission.
Persists immutable event evidence within this workspace. Retry the exact source and body. Waiting workflows read this evidence durably.

Requires `workflows.author`. Tests an exact version with example inputs, capability replies and expected outputs. Evaluation does not call connected systems. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Cancel a running Code Step evaluation

post.description: Stops computation and prevents new capability requests. Actions already admitted may still complete and require reconciliation.

get.summary: Read replenishment rules and a page of stock choices
get.description: Returns up to 50 stock choices. Search by SKU or filter to a position or connection. Continue with nextCursor and the same filters. Rule readiness includes the current stock for every configured rule, independently of this page.

post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Reviews a stock position, supplier and quantity limits. Target stock must exceed the minimum. Reuse the exact ID and body when retrying.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Checks up to 25 stock positions before activating rules. Each position shows current stock, whether an active rule already covers it, what the first check would propose and who approves. Nothing changes.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Activates up to 25 reviewed rules, each for exactly one stock position. Each rule succeeds or fails on its own; an existing rule is never replaced. Resend the same items to retry: activated rules are returned unchanged and never duplicated.

get.summary: Read workflow coverage for a record
get.description: Returns the workflows that can cover a stock position, with the same readiness, blockers and next action as the workflow itself, scoped to that record.

post.summary: Check low stock and start replenishment
post.description: Reads current stock on the server and starts the activated version when stock is below its minimum. Reuse the request ID after an uncertain response.

get.description: Returns recorded stock, supplier, policy decision, current purchase-order status and independent verification. Responding to a pending proposal requires `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond` and follows the workspace independent approval setting.

post.summary: Approve or reject a replenishment proposal
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond`. The approver decides on the exact proposal under the workspace independent approval setting. Current stock, activation and policy are checked again before creating the order.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can inspect published versions and activation status. Viewing a workflow never activates it.
Read published steps, versions, prerequisites and historical grants. Process versions show the exact order of decisions, actions, waits and verification.

Returns the 50 most recent runs with subject, actor, trigger and step evidence, and the names of the people who started them. Process runs show their current state and recorded outputs. Execution and verification results are separate.

post.summary: Start or schedule a workflow run
post.description: Requires `workflows.triggers.manage`. Submits typed signal evidence for an exact version and resource. Reuse the source ID and complete body on retry. Starts do not grant execution authority. Schedules start once at the time specified by the version.

post.summary: Cancel a scheduled start or open workflow handoff

post.description: Requires `playbooks.activate`. Activates supported Resolution versions for your own principal and explicit orders on one connection. Other definitions remain available for review. Review the exact digest, scope and approval behavior. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response. Conflicting, overlapping or stale grants return 409; revoked records cannot be restored.

Requires `workflows.publish`. Lets a built-in workflow start a run for each new case of its issue type. Runs act as the caller; every change still needs policy approval under the workspace rules. Review the exact version digest and policy version. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response. A second active activation returns 409.

Requires `playbooks.activate` or `procurement.manage`. Prevents future admission under this artifact. Repeated revocation is safe. Revocation preserves historical grants and does not undo already-dispatched work.

get.description: Returns templates from installed adapters with what each needs before it can run, its readiness and its activation status here.

post.summary: Add a template to this workspace
post.description: Requires `workflows.publish`. Publishes the template’s reviewed version here so it can be configured. Repeating the request is safe. Adding a template never activates it.

get.summary: List what workflows can use in this workspace
get.description: Returns triggers, step types, subjects, data sources, actions and result checks from installed adapters. Entries that cannot run here are included with the reason.

post.summary: Check a draft without saving it
post.description: Checks a saved draft or supplied content. Diagnostics name the step and field to fix. Errors block publishing; warnings describe what cannot run in this workspace yet. Validation changes nothing.

get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read drafts. Drafts never run and grant no access to connected systems.

post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Starts a draft from scratch, from supplied content, or from a published version to edit it. Editing a published workflow never changes that version. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

put.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Saves against the revision you loaded. If someone else saved first, the request returns 409 and nothing is overwritten. Reuse the same save ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Publish a draft as a new version
post.description: Requires `workflows.publish`. Publishes the exact revision you reviewed as an immutable version. Publishing does not activate the workflow or grant it access to anything. Retrying the same revision returns the same version.
Requires `workflows.author`. Discards a draft you no longer need. Discarding again is safe. Published drafts are kept.

get.summary: Check whether workflows can be described here
get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. Describing workflows needs an EU model route with zero data retention. When none is configured, `reason` explains what an administrator must set up.

post.summary: Start a draft from a description
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe what should happen and get a new draft with an explanation of each step, the assumptions made and open questions. Each question names the step and field to fill in. The draft uses only what this workspace has installed and still needs review, testing and publishing: generation never publishes, activates, approves or starts a workflow. The model may be asked up to three times; remaining problems are returned as diagnostics. If the model fails, times out or returns nothing usable, the request returns 503, no draft is created, and you can try again. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Propose a change from an instruction
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe a change to the revision you loaded. The response is a proposal with step-level changes; the draft is unchanged until the proposal is accepted. Returns 409 if the draft changed since you loaded it, and 503 with nothing changed if the model fails or times out. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

Requires `workflows.author`. Saves the proposed content as a new draft revision. If the draft changed after the proposal was made, the request returns 409 and nothing is applied. Accepting never publishes. Reuse the same save ID after an uncertain response.
Requires `workflows.author`. Discards a proposal. The draft is unchanged. Rejecting again is safe.

post.summary: Suggest a Code Step from a description
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Describe a calculation and get TypeScript source, returned fields, grants and example cases for the Code Step editor. The source uses only values available at that step and requests only the reads and actions directly after it. Nothing is saved. Returns 503 with nothing changed if the model fails or times out. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

get.summary: List how a draft was generated
get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read the model route, token usage, attempts and outcome of each request for this draft, newest first. Prompts are stored only as a hash. These records show authorship; they don’t approve anything.

get.summary: List saved test cases and their results
get.description: Requires `workflows.read`. People can read saved test cases and whether each passed on the current draft revision. A case without a result has not run on this revision yet.

put.summary: Save test cases for a draft
put.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Replaces the saved test cases against the revision you loaded (0 before any are saved). If someone else saved first, the request returns 409. Retrying the same body after an uncertain response is safe.

post.summary: Run saved test cases on the current revision
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Runs every saved case that has no passing or running result on this draft revision. Call it after saving the draft and before publishing. Repeating the call is safe. Tests use example replies and never contact connected systems.

get.summary: Suggest example data for a test
get.description: Returns a case filled from the declared fields, cases from recent runs of the published workflow this draft edits that you can read, and scenarios from installed adapters. Nothing is saved.

post.summary: Test a draft with example data
post.description: Requires `workflows.author`. Runs the current draft revision with a saved or unsaved case. The run uses the production workflow interpreter with example replies instead of connected systems, Action Admission or action adapters. A passing test grants no activation or approval. Poll the run until it finishes. Reuse the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

get.summary: Read a test run you started
get.description: Shows each step the run reached with its values, the path taken and where it would wait for a person.

post.summary: Cancel a test run you started
post.description: Stops the run, including any Code Step. Cancelling a finished run returns it unchanged.
Requires `procurement.manage`. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Creates a draft with immutable lines and provenance. Luma-owned orders support audited lifecycle changes. External ownership requires an external reference and prevents local lifecycle changes. Reuse the ID and body on retry.

get.summary: Read a purchase order and its lifecycle history

get.description: Returns the supplier, its purchasing-system link, every purchase order with its stage and progress, and recent supplier messages. Stages come from recorded evidence: confirmation and receipt are read from the purchasing system or recorded from supplier messages; receipt only from the purchasing system.

post.summary: Link a supplier to its purchasing-system record
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Links the supplier to a supplier in a connected purchasing system, or removes the link, and sets how many hours the supplier has to confirm a sent order. Provide the current revision. The purchasing-system supplier is read again before it is linked.

get.description: Connections that requested supplier or purchase-order access, with what they are currently allowed to do.

get.summary: List suppliers in a purchasing system
get.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Reads up to 100 suppliers per page from the connection, for linking. Nothing is stored.

One stage per order (draft, sending, awaiting confirmation, confirmed, changed, partially received, received, closed or cancelled), with the earliest expected date of outstanding units, how many items need attention and who acts next.

get.summary: Read a purchase order record with its supplier lifecycle
get.description: Returns the order, lifecycle history, its submission to a purchasing system, supplier messages and extraction attempts, every commitment with its source, purchasing-system reads, follow-up responses and derived progress. A draft, a sent order, a supplier confirmation and a booked goods receipt are separate milestones; only the purchasing system establishes receipt.

post.description: Reads the order in its purchasing system and records any new confirmation or receipt. Requires `procurement.read`.

post.summary: Request approval to send an order to the supplier
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Asks for approval to place this draft or open order in the supplier’s linked purchasing system, with a requested delivery date. Someone else with `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond` must approve. Every line’s SKU must be linked to a purchasing-system item. After approval Luma places the order once and verifies it with an independent read; the purchasing system sends it to the supplier. Reuse the ID and body after an uncertain response. Requests expire after 24 hours.

post.summary: Approve or reject sending an order
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage` and `decisions.respond`, plus any app permission the purchasing capability declares. An authorized person approves or rejects the exact submission under the workspace independent approval setting. Approval dispatches it as the requester after their membership, the order and the supplier link are checked again.
The requester dispatches an approved submission that has not been sent. Repeated calls return the recorded attempt.
Reads the purchasing system to settle whether an uncertain submission created the order. It never sends the order again.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Records a supplier message for this order. When an EU model route is configured, Luma lists the commitments it states, each with the exact words it came from; changes, uncertain readings and conditions wait for review. The same message, by message ID or content, is recorded once. Text is removed after the retention period.
Retries reading a message whose earlier attempts were unavailable or failed.
Requires `procurement.manage`. Removes the subject and text now. The sender, time, content digest and recorded commitments remain; quotes can no longer be shown.

post.summary: Record or correct a supplier commitment
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Records a confirmed quantity, promised date, shipment or condition by selecting the words in a supplier message, or corrects an earlier commitment with a reason. Corrections add a commitment; nothing is overwritten. Receipt cannot be recorded here.

post.summary: Confirm or reject an extracted commitment
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Confirms or rejects a commitment that needed review. `acceptChange` also accepts a quantity or date change.

post.summary: Respond to a change or missed deadline
post.description: Requires `procurement.manage`. Accepts a supplier change, or records a follow-up with when Luma should check again (within 60 days). The key must be one of the order’s current attention items.

Requires `procurement.manage`. Moves drafts to open or cancelled, and open orders to closed or cancelled. Provide the current revision and a reason. Reuse the command ID and body on retry. Closing records completion; it does not record a warehouse receipt.

get.summary: Read stock, products and issues around a purchase order
get.description: For each line, the canonical SKU it resolves to, current stock per location and source (never added together), and other draft or open purchase orders for the SKU. Also returns related issues and, for replenishment drafts, the run evidence that created it: stock at the check, the rule’s minimum and target, approval and independent verification. Up to 20 positions per SKU and 50 issues.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.summary: Read stock for the SKUs a supplier provides
get.description: The SKUs on this supplier’s purchase orders (up to 50, most recent first) with current stock per location and source, units on this supplier’s draft and open orders, and related issues.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: Returns each connected mailbox with its reading state and the rules that decide which messages Luma reads. Luma reads only messages that match a rule.

put.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Fails with 409 when `expectedRevision` is not current.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Luma then reads matching messages from the mailbox's backfill window. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Luma stops reading new matching messages; threads already read stay.
Requires `messages.manage`. Schedules a read within seconds; the response does not wait for it.

get.description: Lists threads read from connected mailboxes, newest activity first. `overdue` lists threads whose reply deadline passed; `review` lists threads with document facts to review.
Returns messages with their source identity, linked records, internal notes, the thread timeline, documents and replies.

get.summary: List threads linked to a record
get.description: Requires `messages.read` and permission to read the record. Suggested links are not included.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. The owner must be a workspace member who can read messages. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Null returns to the automatic deadline. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. A new inbound message reopens a closed thread. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Notes stay in Luma and are never sent. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Link a thread to a record
post.description: Requires `messages.manage` and permission to read the record. Confirms a suggested link to the same record. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Luma does not add the same automatic link again. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.
Requires `messages.manage`. Removes the text and attachment content; metadata, links and reviewed facts remain.

get.summary: Read a document and its facts
get.description: Returns the document content beside the facts proposed from it. Each fact cites its page, text span or cells.

post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Retries a failed read; reviewed facts are kept.
Requires `messages.manage`. The locator must point to text or cells in the document. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Confirm, correct or reject a fact
post.description: Requires `messages.manage`. Facts that need correction cannot be confirmed unchanged. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

Requires `messages.send`. Builds the draft from the current state of the linked records and cites each one; missing or stale evidence is stated in the draft. Retry with the same ID and body after an uncertain response.

put.description: Requires `messages.send`. Only drafts can change; fails with 409 when `expectedRevision` is not current.

post.summary: Send a reply or request approval
post.description: Requires `messages.send`. Replies that confirm a date or quantity, mention money, or fall under the workspace rule need approval from someone else; others are sent at once. Sending is confirmed by a fresh read of the thread.
Requires `decisions.respond` and the mailbox app’s send permission. The requester cannot approve their own reply.
Requires `messages.send`; only the requester can send. Sends at most once; repeating returns the recorded result.

post.summary: Check whether a reply was sent
post.description: Requires `messages.send`. Reads the thread again; never sends.
Requires `messages.send`. Only drafts and replies waiting for approval can be discarded.

get.description: People who can manage issues can find up to 50 runs for a case. Pass nextCursor as after to continue; IDs provide stable page ordering. Refresh from the first page to discover newly recorded runs.

post.description: People who can manage issues record a run ID, diagnosis revision, resolution version and reason. Reuse the run ID for automated steps. Exact retries return the original record; conflicting IDs return 409.

Append cause assessments, repairs, interventions, edits, outcomes or recurrence links. Use codes and incident evidence references. Model hypotheses remain suspected. Verified outcomes require the incident’s authoritative verification. Exact retries return the original event.

get.description: People who can manage issues can export the original context, ordered operator records, bound steps, execution and all verification attempts. A pending attempt without completion has no known result. Execution acceptance does not establish business success.
Returns an immutable proposal, its current policy result and permitted decisions. Unavailable capabilities cannot be approved. Manual recommendations remain in the case investigation.

post.summary: Check current facts for a resolution proposal
post.description: Checks current source facts and prepares a current proposal where supported. Existing approvals and execution records are preserved. Changed conditions require review; provider unavailability can be retried.

post.summary: Approve, reject, escalate or close a case
post.description: Use a unique commandId and the current case, diagnosis, proposal and policy versions from review. Exact retries return the committed receipt. Conflicts return 409. Approval records a decision; it does not mean execution or verification succeeded. Closing requires issues.manage, a reason of 1–1000 characters and optional tenant-owned evidence references. It blocks pending proposals but does not cancel a change already in flight. Manual closure is separate from verified resolution.

get.description: After a timeout, read the receipt using the original command ID or retry the identical request. Receipts are visible to their submitting actor.
Returns persisted execution and canonical resolution separately from workflow phase. An unavailable workflow service does not imply success or no activity.
Returns up to 100 persisted events, ordered by timestamp and ID. Reuse cursors with the same organization, case and page size. Refresh from the first page and deduplicate by ID as events arrive.

post.description: People who can manage issues append versioned eligibility, attribution, environment, incorrect-action or measured partner-baseline assessments. Evidence must belong to the incident. Environment is immutable. Expected revision prevents concurrent lost updates; exact retries return the original fact. These facts grant no execution authority.

get.description: People who can read issues can read up to 100 immutable measurement facts after a revision. Follow nextRevision for more; revision identifies the current head.

Returns current attention and active counts, up to five decisions ordered by severity then oldest request, and verified resolutions in the selected rolling window [start, end). Connection freshness requires observations for every permitted read capability within 24 hours. The measurement summary counts live incidents first detected in the selected window. Exact automation is withheld for unknown eligibility, human attribution or environment; verifiedResolutions retains its completion-time window. Counts describe persisted cases; fresh observations do not establish complete source coverage.
Lists domain-owned definitions. Order definitions use v1 query semantics; other families use v2 with coverage and typed cohorts per metric.

post.summary: Read selected operational metrics and matching records
post.description: Reads cases, monitored stock, purchase orders, connection health and evidence-backed resolution outcomes in one consistent, current read. Select metric IDs explicitly. Filters must be supported by every selected metric. Each metric returns its first page of records; pass a metric’s nextCursor as cursor to read the records after that page. Pages read current data, so records can join or leave between pages; deduplicate by ID. A cursor from another request returns 422. Resolution alone accepts environment and a 24-hour or seven-day first-detection window; other families describe current state. Null values, unknown classification and unavailable coverage are distinct from zero.

cursor.description: A metric’s nextCursor. That metric lists the records after the previous page, read from current data; the other metrics return their first page.

offset.description: Records paged past before this page. It labels the page; records may have changed since earlier pages.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the records after this page. Null when no more records match.

post.summary: Read several metric views in one request
post.description: Reads up to four parts, each an order (v1) or operational (v2) metric query, with the same rules as those endpoints, and returns them in request order. A part that fails carries its own status and error; the other parts are unaffected. Each part returns its first page of records; read later pages through the part’s own query endpoint. nextRefreshAt is the earliest boundary across the parts that were read.

cursor.description: A metric’s nextCursor. That metric lists the records after the previous page, read from current data; the other metrics return their first page.
A metric’s nextCursor. That metric lists the records after the previous page, read from current data; the other metrics return their first page.

nextRefreshAt.description: Earliest refresh boundary across the parts that were read.
Next deadline or freshness boundary. Refresh current metrics at this time, even if no change event arrives.

offset.description: Records paged past before this page. It labels the page; records may have changed since earlier pages.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the records after this page. Null when no more records match.

offset.description: Records paged past before this page. It labels the page; records may have changed since earlier pages.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the records after this page. Null when no more records match.

get.description: Lists versioned counting rules, supported filters, permissions and drill-down semantics for canonical order metrics.

post.summary: Read order totals and their matching records
post.description: Returns open, overdue and attention counts with a page of matching orders for each, from one consistent, current read. Null totals mean incomplete source coverage; observedCount counts only known matching orders. Pass a metric’s nextCursor as cursor to read the orders after that page; pages read current data, so deduplicate by ID. A cursor from another request returns 422. Windows filter accepted source update times using [updatedFrom, updatedBefore) UTC instants. Requests accept only registered fields, never executable code.

cursor.description: A metric’s nextCursor. That metric lists the records after the previous page, read from current data; the other metrics return their first page.

nextRefreshAt.description: Next deadline or freshness boundary. Refresh current metrics at this time, even if no change event arrives.

offset.description: Records paged past before this page. It labels the page; records may have changed since earlier pages.

nextCursor.description: Pass as cursor to read the records after this page. Null when no more records match.

post.summary: Assign or clear a case owner
post.description: Changes responsibility with an optimistic revision. Assignment is audited and grants no approval or execution authority.

get.description: Filter attention, active work or history by class, severity and state. Results sort by severity, oldest attention request or detection, then ID. Use the returned cursor with the same filters. Refresh from the first page as cases change.

Returns persisted observation and verification references ordered by immutable ID, including evidence outside the current diagnosis. Pages default to 25 references and allow at most 100. Reuse cursors only for the same organization, case and page size. As evidence arrives, refresh from the first page and deduplicate by ID. Completeness is unknown unless explicitly recorded for the observation. A null source update time means unknown, regardless of observation freshness.

Returns the current persisted investigation and up to 100 evidence references. Use the evidence endpoint to read further historical references. Recommendations require review; they do not authorize execution. Unavailable cases return not found.

get.summary: Read the Luma support view in this browser
get.description: Returns the read-only support view this browser holds: the workspace, the member it shows and when it ends. Inactive when there is none or it ended, with the reason it just ended.

post.description: Exchanges the single-use token from a staff console link, within two minutes, for a support view cookie. While the cookie is present, workspace routes show the viewed member’s access read-only and refuse every change.
Ends the support view this browser holds, records its end and clears its cookie.

get.description: Returns sign-ins, failed sign-in attempts and security changes for your own account, newest first, 20 per page. Events are kept for one year; IP addresses and devices for 90 days.

put.description: Stores the interface language Luma uses for email to you, such as invitations, notifications and account notices. The web app calls this after you pick a language.

get.description: Includes workspaces where your membership is suspended. Their `membershipStatus` is `suspended`, and their tenant routes return 403 until the membership is reactivated.

post.description: Creates an EU organization with you as its owner. Other regions are unavailable.

get.description: Returns your membership, role and effective permissions. Changes to your role apply on the next request.

post.summary: Add a registered user to an organization
post.description: Requires `members.manage`. Only owners can grant ownership, and others can only assign roles whose permissions they hold.

patch.description: Requires `members.manage`. Only owners change ownership; others can only assign roles, and change members, whose permissions they hold. The last active owner cannot be demoted.

delete.description: The last active owner cannot be removed or demoted.

get.summary: Check whether your settings command committed
Read workspace settings and your email preferences

patch.summary: Update the workspace name and display timezone

patch.description: Only workspace owners may change this mode. Observe-only preserves reads and proposals while refusing provider writes.

patch.summary: Set when approval is needed and who may approve
patch.description: Requires `workspace.approval_policy.manage`. Always requiring approval includes low-risk changes. Independent approval requires a different person; it is off while fewer than two members have access. Platform denials and required reviews still apply. Changes invalidate previous policy reviews.

get.summary: Read your Home layout and pinned pages
get.description: Layouts are personal: each member arranges their own Home and sidebar pins in each workspace. A null Home uses the default modules.

put.summary: Save your Home layout and pinned pages
put.description: Send the revision you last read. The save is rejected with 409 when another session saved a newer layout; read it again before retrying.

post.summary: Queue a test email to your account

post.description: Sending an invitation does not grant access. The invitation is bound to an active role other than Owner whose permissions you hold. An existing pending invitation must be resent or revoked; existing members cannot be invited.
Resending replaces the previous link and starts a new seven-day expiry.

get.description: Returns until when Luma support may open read-only views of this workspace, and pending requests from Luma support.

put.description: Lets Luma support open read-only views of this workspace as a member, for 24, 72 or 168 hours from now. Replaces an earlier end time. Views can’t change anything, and each one appears in Activity.

post.description: Ends support access now. Open support views end on their next request.

post.summary: Approve or decline a Luma support access request
post.description: Approving allows support access for the requested duration from now, or keeps a later end time. A request that lapsed or was answered returns 409.

post.summary: Review an invitation for your signed-in email
Accept a single-use invitation for your signed-in email

get.summary: List workspace roles and the permissions they can grant
get.description: Returns built-in and custom roles with member counts, and the permission catalog including permissions declared by installed apps. Any member can read roles.

post.description: Requires `roles.manage`. You can only grant permissions you hold, unless you are an owner. Reusing `x-command-id` returns the original result.

patch.description: Send the revision you last read; a newer revision returns 409. Changes apply to every member with the role on their next request. Built-in roles cannot be changed.

post.description: Reassign every member first; a role in use returns 409. Archiving revokes pending invitations for the role.

get.description: Lists up to 100 recent changes to the role and its member assignments, newest first.

post.description: Requires `connections.manage`. The connection remains pending until a successful permission check.

patch.description: Owners may impose observe-only or restore workspace inheritance. A connection cannot enable writes in an observe-only workspace.

post.description: Replaces credentials and clears verified permissions. Check the connection again to restore access. Also reconnects a connection whose provider revoked access, keeping its ID, mappings and history; a disconnected connection returns 409. Use the latest connection version.
Deletes stored credentials and stops further use. Does not revoke provider tokens or cancel requests already sent. Install a new connection to reconnect.

get.summary: List available apps and workspace installations
get.description: Includes the permissions each app declares, the access it requests, the scopes granted to each installation and roles that hold its permissions.

post.summary: Install an app in this workspace
post.description: Requires `apps.manage` and every scope the app requests: you can only grant access you have. Send the requested scopes you reviewed; a changed request returns 409. Use null for a first installation or the current version to reinstall. Reinstalling restores no role permissions.

post.summary: Approve access an upgraded app requests
post.description: Requires `apps.manage` and each approved scope. Until approved, the app keeps working with the scopes granted earlier.

Requires `apps.manage`. Stops new app operations, deletes connection credentials and scope grants, and removes the app’s permissions from every role. Historical records remain. Requests already dispatched may finish.

get.summary: Check whether the API is running
Check whether the API is ready to serve requests
get.description: Returns 200 when ready and 503 when temporarily unavailable.
Browse provider names and categories. Filter by storefront or ERP.
Look up a provider by its ID. Returns 404 if the provider is not in the catalog.
Finds an order by its exact connection and source ID. No IDs means it has not been mapped. Two IDs indicate an ambiguous mapping; do not select one automatically.

Searches current records in your workspace, most recently observed first. Filter by connection to inspect one source. Each page holds up to 50 records with source identity, freshness and coverage; pass `nextCursor` as `cursor` to read the next page. A cursor from a different search returns 400. Customer and return coverage is unavailable.
Returns the current source snapshots and confirmed related records. Each source remains separate so differing or uncertain mappings are visible.

Lists fulfillment orders and shipments as each connected source currently reports them. `attention` returns held, delayed and failed fulfillments; `held` returns open work stopped by a source hold; `delayed` returns open work past its fulfill-by date or without progress for `stalledAfterHours`, and shipments with a reported delivery problem or past their estimated delivery; `open` returns work still expected; `in_transit` returns shipped, undelivered shipments. Search matches order numbers, tracking numbers, location names and source order or fulfillment IDs. Mirrored work in different systems stays separate. Results contain up to `limit` fulfillments (at most 50) with counts per view; `nextCursor` continues the same filters, sort and evaluation time.

Returns one fulfillment with its lines, order, up to 50 of the order’s other fulfillments, up to 50 observed source states (newest first), linked issues, workflow runs and recent Luma activity. A workflow run’s `progressObservedAt` is the first later read showing the order shipped or its work completed; a method correction or an accepted source request alone does not establish progress.

Read up to 50 source summaries with separately reported stages. Transfer and shipment quantities do not augment stock balances. Signals require active grants and complete evidence observed within five minutes; a past arrival estimate establishes only that receipt is unconfirmed.

Read one source projection, exact line identities, historical location snapshots, up to 20 observations and 50 explicit relationships per type. Null collections are unavailable. Procurement links require procurement.read and an exact connection-scoped external reference. No stock, receiving or claim action is executed.

Search SKUs and locations and compare current stock quantities by source. Quantities are never added across sources. Null means unknown. Results contain up to 50 positions; nextCursor continues the same filters. Source filters select positions while retaining all sources for comparison.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: Compare sources for one SKU, location and unit. Includes up to 100 observed snapshots and 50 entries per related record type. Orders and purchase orders relate to the SKU; they do not confirm location allocation or incoming supply. Incoming quantities and distinct provider stock states remain unknown until reported. Location activity, item activation and tracking are separate facts; quantities do not establish sellability.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.
Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: List SKUs from the connected catalogs and compare each source’s title, status, listing, price and barcode. No source is treated as authoritative. `differs` returns SKUs whose sources disagree; `missing` returns SKUs absent from at least one catalog source; `unlinked` returns SKUs with an unlinked SKU of the same code in another source. Prices are compared only within the same reported currency. Results contain up to `limit` SKUs (at most 50) with counts per view; nextCursor continues the same filters.

Compare one SKU across sources and see what depends on it: other variants, up to 50 observed listing snapshots, stock positions, units ordered in the last 30 days per source, orders, purchase orders and issues (up to 50 each). Sales are not added across sources because systems can mirror the same order. Purchase orders are commitments, not confirmed incoming stock.

bundleContext.description: Catalog context of a known bundle parent. Its timestamp is independent of the stock read and does not establish physical component stock.

get.description: Lists current orders from your connected sources. Search matches order numbers, source order IDs, SKU text on order lines and source SKU IDs. Filter by status, payment, source, customer, placed or updated time, or a saved view. Filtering by customer also needs access to customers and returns 403 without it. Outstanding, overdue and needs-you views count the same orders as the order metrics. Pass `count=exact` to include the total number of matches; otherwise `totalCount` is null. Results use `nextCursor` for the following page; a cursor is only valid with the filters and sort that produced it, and any other cursor returns 400 with a message to start from the first page.

schema.description: Request the exact number of matches. Without this option, totalCount is null.
Imported customer ID: only orders the source attributes to this customer. Requires access to customers.

get.description: Returns each source’s current facts for one order, where they differ, fulfillment progress, observed source history, linked issues and workflow runs, and recent Luma activity. Customer and payment details stay in the connected app and are not part of this response.

bundleGroup.description: Merchandising group of this component. It is not an additional stock or fulfillment line. Omitted means unread; null means standalone.

taxIncluded.description: Whether the unit price includes tax, as the source states it.

quantity.description: Originally ordered units, including subsequent reductions.

currentQuantity.description: Current units excluding removed and refunded units; null when not reported.

cancelledQuantity.description: Reduced units, including removals or refunds when the source reports them; null when unknown.

kind.description: Shipment or fulfillment work, when reported by the source.

remainingQuantity.description: Provider-reported outstanding work; null when not reported.

bundleGroup.description: Merchandising group of this component. It is not an additional stock or fulfillment line. Omitted means unread; null means standalone.

taxIncluded.description: Whether the unit price includes tax, as the source states it.

quantity.description: Originally ordered units, including subsequent reductions.

kind.description: Shipment or fulfillment work, when reported by the source.

get.description: Returns the editable record and addresses when Luma orders are released for this workspace. Returns null before intake.

patch.description: Checks the reviewed version and Luma lifecycle and line authority, then atomically saves the record, changed evidence and an audit receipt. Reuse the command ID for an identical retry.

post.summary: Accept a Shopify order into Luma
post.description: Copies a current Shopify order into one Luma record. Requires import management. Repeated intake returns the existing record. Does not change source authority.

get.description: List returns imported from connected stores, and refunds that no return settles, with their stage and refund state. `action` returns need a person: a request to review, units to refund, a failed refund payment or a return to close. `waiting` returns wait for items or a processing refund payment; `done` returns are closed, declined, cancelled or refunded. `refund.refunded` sums successful refund payments only; pending and failed payments are reported separately and never count as money returned. `sources` lists each commerce connection and whether it shares returns with Luma. Search matches the return name, order number, return reason and source IDs. Results contain up to `limit` records (at most 50) with counts per view and stage; nextCursor continues the same filters and sorting.

Read one return with its items, reasons, receipt and refund quantities, refunds with every payment attempt, the order it belongs to, other returns of that order and up to 50 observed snapshots. The ID of a refund that settles a return resolves to that return. Store returns are read-only here; work them in a return case, and approve, receive and refund them in the source store.
Reads configured hours anchored to recorded case events. Configuration alone does not turn on automatic monitoring.

post.description: Saves a revision-checked policy. Exact command retries retain the original version. Activate Return step follow-up in Workflows to monitor automatically.

get.description: Reads owned waits, escalation and earlier occurrences without refreshing provider evidence.

post.description: Independently rereads financial evidence and records actual receipt and inspection progress. It executes no provider write.

get.description: Reads the operation, independent fulfillment and payment proof, and explicitly mapped replacement choices.

post.summary: Verify exchange consistency in both systems
post.description: Independently reads Shopify and Wawi. Completes the case only when returned stock, exactly one replacement order, its reservation, price and actual payment agree. A failed later check reopens owned work. Executes no provider write.
Freezes one native request, process, cancellation or payment hold release for independent approval. All attempts retain the same case operation. Uncertain sent writes are checked without redispatch.

post.summary: Choose how to handle replacement availability
post.description: Records wait, different item or refund with an owner. The choice does not send a provider write. A different item or refund requires independently approved and freshly verified cancellation first.

post.summary: Hand off a cancelled exchange to refund
post.description: After fresh cancellation proof, changes the proposal to refund while preserving physical inspection and restock quantities. Refunding remains a separately approved settlement.
A current independent approver responds to the frozen step. Execution uses the requester’s rechecked authority.
Resumes the same durable execution identity. A sent uncertain effect is reconciled without creating a second replacement.
Independently reads the exact native replacement, fulfillment and financial outcome. Provider acceptance does not prove payment or case closure.

get.description: Reads recorded physical and financial actions. Managers with a restock proposal also receive current Wawi warehouse choices for explicitly mapped items.

post.description: Freezes the provider-calculated refund or the inspected resale units at an explicitly mapped warehouse. Refunds never restock goods. An independent approver must authorize the exact action.
A current independent approver responds to the frozen action. Approval dispatches once as the requester after their authority and case facts are checked again.
The requester sends an approved action through Action Admission. Repeated calls do not duplicate the provider effect.
Independently reads the exact stock change or refund payment. Pending, failed and uncertain outcomes stay distinct. This command never sends a provider write.

get.description: Searches persisted return cases by case, order, source identity or item. Customer filtering also requires customers.read and follows source order mappings. No provider is called. The cursor is bound to the tenant and filters.

Requires `returns.read`. Lists the order’s return cases and, for each source of the order, how many units of every line are ordered, already in return cases or in store returns no case works, and still returnable. Each unit counts once: a store return that a case works counts only through that case.

post.description: Requires `returns.manage`. Opens a return case on lines of one source of the order, with whole units, a reason per line and an optional note. Pass `sourceReturnId` to work a store return of that source; one open case works a store return. Lines can’t claim more units than are still returnable. The ID is the idempotency key: reuse it with the same body after an uncertain response.

get.description: Requires `returns.read`. Reads a return case with its lines, the receipt, inspection and proposed resolution with who decided them and on which evidence, the case history, and the latest request to create the return in the order’s system.

post.description: Requires `returns.manage`. Assigns receiving and inspecting to a current member who can manage returns, or clears the assignee with null. Every change names a new `commandId` and the case’s current `expectedRevision`.

Requires `returns.manage`. Records the received units of every case line, never more than requested, with optional evidence. A new receipt replaces the earlier one and clears the inspection and proposal that relied on it; the history keeps both.
Requires `returns.manage`. Judges every received unit of each line as resellable or damaged. Units requested but not received are missing. Needs a recorded receipt and clears an earlier proposal.

Requires `returns.manage`. Proposes a refund, exchange, store credit or rejection, with the units of each line to restock. Only units inspected as resellable can be restocked, and a rejection restocks nothing. A proposal changes nothing in the store.
Requires `returns.manage`. Cancels the case with a reason; its units can be returned again. Refused while the return is being created in the order’s system.

get.description: Requires `returns.manage`. Reads the warehouses and return reasons of the system the case’s order came from, to create the return there.

post.summary: Request a return in the order’s system
post.description: Requires `returns.manage`. Asks for approval to create this case’s return, with its lines, the chosen warehouse and one return reason, in the system the order came from. Someone else with `returns.manage`, `decisions.respond` and the app’s permission approves. Luma then creates it once and verifies it with an independent read; an uncertain result is only ever checked by reading. Observe-only workspaces and connections record the request and send nothing. Requests expire after 24 hours. Reuse the ID and body after an uncertain response.

post.summary: Approve or reject creating a return
post.description: Requires `returns.manage` and `decisions.respond`, plus the app permission of the creating capability. Someone other than the requester approves or rejects the exact request. Approval creates the return as the requester after their membership and the case are checked again.
Requires `returns.manage`. The requester creates an approved return that was not sent. Repeated calls return the recorded attempt.
Requires `returns.manage`. Reads the order’s system to settle whether an uncertain request created the return. It never sends the request again.

get.description: List customer profiles imported from connected stores. Each profile belongs to one connection and source customer; profiles are never merged across stores, and names or email addresses do not establish identity. Name, email and phone are null unless the source shares contact details (`shared.contact`). `orderCount` and `amountSpent` are what the source reports. Search matches the name, email address, phone number and source customer ID. `externalId` with `connectionId` finds one source customer. `sources` lists each commerce connection and whether it shares customers with Luma. Results contain up to `limit` profiles (at most 50) with `totalCount` matches; nextCursor continues the same filters and sorting.

missingSince.description: When a complete read of the source first no longer found this customer; null while the source still has them. Luma removes customers that stay missing for 30 days.

get.description: Read one imported customer profile with its address, when the source shares addresses, and the connection it came from. Order history is read live through the connected app.

missingSince.description: When a complete read of the source first no longer found this customer; null while the source still has them. Luma removes customers that stay missing for 30 days.

get.description: Lists connection-pair rules for SKU codes and ERP order references to Shopify orders, with their last check, total links and any reason they are waiting or blocked.

put.description: Requires Manage imports. Creates a rule with revision zero, or enables or disables an existing rule using its current revision. Each save is audited and enabled rules run with the caller’s current access. Disabling stops future links and keeps existing links. SKU rules require unique normalized codes and compatible units; order rules match an ERP order’s explicit external order number, as JTL and Cin7 report it, to one selected Shopify store. Every application rechecks current evidence and preserves mapping history.

post.description: Requires Manage imports. Shows counts and up to 20 examples for the selected record type and connections. Does not link records. Duplicate codes or references, conflicting mappings or units, manually separated records and stale or missing evidence are skipped.

get.description: Shows, for each connection and record type, whether Luma is importing history, keeping records in sync, retrying or waiting for someone. Includes imported record counts, the creation-date range Luma holds, any source history limit, the last successful sync and recent runs. A record type is `not_requested` when the connection does not include it and `not_granted` when the source did not grant it.

post.description: Requires `sync.manage`. Pauses or resumes a sync, retries now, requests a full check against the source (`reconcile`) or imports the history again (`reimport`). Resuming, retrying and re-importing continue with the caller’s access. Re-importing keeps every imported record; unchanged records are recognized and not duplicated. Commands are idempotent.

get.description: Lists the source records that represent one SKU, location or order, how each was linked, and possible matches in other sources. Suggestions share a SKU code or an ERP order’s marketplace order reference. Configured automatic linking rules may apply unambiguous matches; other suggestions require review.

post.description: Requires `sync.manage`. Confirms that another SKU, location or order is the same record (`link`), or separates one connection’s source from it (`unlink`). Luma applies the change in the background, keeps the previous mapping as history and re-projects affected projections. Order links keep each source’s lines and shipments separate and preserve old references. Poll the returned request for its outcome.

get.description: Returns whether a link or unlink request is waiting, running, completed or failed, with an explanation when it failed.

get.summary: List decisions that need a person
get.description: List the workspace decisions waiting on a person: issue approvals, manual steps and uncertainty, replenishment purchase-order approvals, purchase orders waiting to be sent, supplier messages to review, supplier changes and overdue confirmations or deliveries, and app-owned stock corrections and fulfillment recoveries. Each item explains why a person is needed, what each response causes, the exact proposed change, evidence freshness and the deadline after which the proposal loses its authority. Items are projections of their owners’ decisions: respond through the owner’s review, which checks the exact proposal, revisions, expiry and approver again. Items sort by urgency (proposals expiring within 30 minutes, then high impact, then the rest), then by deadline, oldest request and ID. Unknown impact is labeled, not ranked low. `response` says what the reader can do; approving needs the permission the owner requires, such as responding to decisions or managing procurement. Requires permission to read issues or procurement. Issue decisions appear only to readers who can read issues, procurement decisions only to readers who can read procurement and app decisions only to readers with the app’s permissions; hidden decisions are left out of the counts too, and record links the reader can’t open are null. `sources` lists the owners the reader can see; owners that failed to answer are unavailable, and their decisions are missing rather than resolved. Results contain up to `limit` items (at most 100); nextCursor continues the same view and filters. An empty queue does not mean operations are healthy.

post.description: Take, hand over or release a decision in the Needs you queue. Taking an unassigned decision or releasing your own needs permission to take decisions; assigning any decision to a current member needs permission to assign decisions. Send the `revision` from the item’s assignment (0 when unassigned); a changed assignment returns 409. The decision must currently need a person. Assigning does not grant approval authority: the owner still checks permissions and applies the workspace’s independent approval setting.

get.description: Counts records for one chart. Timelines place each record in a calendar day or week of `timeZone` by a time its source or Luma recorded: `orders` by the source’s placed time, colored by current status; `cases` by first detection, by issue class. Breakdowns classify current state at `asOf`: `fulfillment` open work by time since its last reported progress, under its first signal (held, past fulfill-by, no progress); `stock` monitored positions against their replenishment minimum; `procurement` purchase orders by stage, overdue or not. Linked orders count once; with `connectionId`, each source’s own records count. Fulfillment work reported by two systems counts once per system. Past states are never reconstructed: a breakdown is today’s state, not history. `coverage` lists each source’s import state; points before imported history are `not_imported`, which means unknown, not zero. `dataThrough` is the oldest complete read across the sources.

schema.description: Calendar days and weeks are counted in this time zone.
Count only records reported by this connection. Charts of Luma records ignore it.

get.summary: List the records behind a chart point
get.description: Lists the records counted in one chart point and series, using the same rules, filters and evaluation time as the chart. Pass the chart’s `asOf` so time-based rules match; `totalCount` then equals the chart value unless records changed since. Results contain up to `limit` records (at most 100) from `offset`; `nextOffset` continues the list.

schema.description: Calendar days and weeks are counted in this time zone.
Count only records reported by this connection. Charts of Luma records ignore it.
A point key from the chart. Omit to list every point.
A series ID from the chart. Omit to list every series.
The chart’s evaluation time, at most 15 minutes old, so time-based rules classify records the same way. Defaults to now.

get.summary: Check whether you can ask Luma here
get.description: Any member can check this. Asking Luma needs the Use Ask Luma permission and an EU model route with zero data retention. Without either, `available` is false and `reason` explains what is missing. `reads` lists the records the assistant can look up for you, based on your role.

post.summary: Ask a question about your workspace
post.description: Answers a question from the orders, issues, stock, fulfillment and returns you can see in this workspace. Luma reads current records for every question, with your access, and never changes anything. Citation markers in `content` link to the records the answer used, with their source and observation time. Send earlier turns in `history` for follow-up questions; Luma does not store conversations. Each answer is limited in reads, length and time; when a limit is reached, `outcome` is `incomplete`. Returns 503 with a reason when the assistant is unavailable here or the model fails, times out or returns nothing usable.

get.description: Returns the authoritative connection for each order and inventory fact group. Unknown or conflicting authority cannot authorize a correction.

post.description: Overrides one fact group or restores its category default with a null connectionId. Requires workspace settings permission, the current revision and a stable commandId for retries. Each change records its actor and before/after override without changing source evidence.

get.description: Returns the latest 100 changes, newest first, including the actor and previous and new overrides.

Authenticated SSE emits resync events with a current progress snapshot every five seconds. Refetch case, review and timeline on each event and reconnect. Last-Event-ID always resynchronizes current state; events are not an audit replay. Sessions and membership are checked before each snapshot. Streams reconnect after one minute. Slow consumers are disconnected. Use the timeline endpoint for persisted history.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Reconnects with a fresh authoritative snapshot.

200.description: SSE resync events. Refetch the subscribed resource when refetch is true.

get.description: Authenticated SSE tells workspace members which areas of data changed. Subscribe before the first query. On resync events with refetch: true, read again the views that depend on a listed topic; on reconnect, read all of them. Topics are limited to areas the member can read; decisions is available to every member. Events contain no records, totals or replay history. Last-Event-ID requests current state. Access is rechecked at least every five seconds and the stream closes when it is lost. Slow consumers disconnect and must resynchronize. Reconciliation lists every readable topic every 30 seconds.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: Reconnects with a fresh authoritative snapshot.

200.description: SSE resync events. Refetch the subscribed resource when refetch is true.
